questions.q: What problem does data augmentation primarily address?
options: It reduces overfitting by exposing the model to realistic, label-preserving variations of existing training images
It increases the number of labels available for a dataset
It speeds up the forward pass of the model
It replaces the need for a validation set
questions.explain: Augmentation generates realistic variations (flips, crops, color changes) of existing images so the model learns to ignore harmless variation rather than overfitting to incidental details — without requiring any new labels.

questions.q: What does `v2.RandomCrop(32, padding=4)` do as part of an augmentation pipeline?
options: It pads the image border by 4 pixels, then crops back to a 32x32 region, slightly shifting the subject's position
It deletes 4 pixels from every image with no replacement
It resizes every image to exactly 4x4 pixels
It converts the image to grayscale
questions.explain: RandomCrop with padding first adds padding around the image, then crops a window of the specified size, effectively shifting the visible content slightly between samples.

questions.q: Why would a horizontal flip be an unsafe augmentation for a task that reads handwritten digits?
options: Digit images cannot be represented as tensors
torchvision does not support flipping grayscale images
A flip can turn one valid digit into a different one (e.g. a 6 into a 9), changing the correct label — it isn't label-preserving for this task
Horizontal flips are always computationally too expensive
questions.explain: An augmentation must preserve the correct label. Flipping a handwritten 6 can make it resemble a 9, which changes what the correct label should be — making the flip unsafe for digit recognition even though it's fine for tasks like cat vs. dog.

questions.q: According to this lesson, should random data augmentation (like RandomHorizontalFlip or ColorJitter) be applied to the validation and test sets?
options: No — validation and test data should reflect the real, unmodified distribution, since augmenting them would make evaluation metrics noisy and unrepresentative
Yes, exactly the same way as the training set
Only ColorJitter should be applied to validation data, never to test data
Augmentation should only ever be applied to the test set, never to training data
questions.explain: Augmentation is meant to diversify training data. Validation and test sets need to reflect the real distribution the model will face in production, so applying random augmentations there would distort the evaluation.

questions.q: In `v2.Compose([..., v2.ToImage(), v2.ToDtype(torch.float32, scale=True), ...])`, what role do `ToImage()` and `ToDtype(..., scale=True)` play?
options: They normalize the image using ImageNet statistics only
They freeze the model's backbone parameters
They are the transforms.v2 way of converting the image into a properly-scaled float tensor, replacing the older ToTensor()
They apply a random crop to the image
questions.explain: In torchvision's transforms.v2 API, ToImage() followed by ToDtype(torch.float32, scale=True) is the standard replacement for the original transforms module's ToTensor(), converting and scaling pixel values into a float tensor.
